input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard operability and focus indicator remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion, each of the four
flows can be completed end-to-end with keyboard alone — no focus traps, no
unreachable controls — and focus indicators are visibly consistent across all
audited surfaces. This epic delivers the code-side fix state that the updated
conformance documentation will describe.

## Scope

- Fix focus-loss and focus-trap defects in the modals and dialogs of the four
  audited flows, per the defect list enumerated in the audit report.
- Make all controls reachable in the audited flows that the audit marked as
  keyboard-unreachable.
- Normalize visible focus indicators across the audited flows so focus state is
  consistent (same visual treatment on equivalent controls) throughout.
- Cover the four audited flows only; flows and screen-reader semantics outside the
  audit scope are explicitly out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed start to finish using
  keyboard input alone, verified by exercising every step of the flow.
- No control in the audited flows is unreachable via keyboard navigation
  (tab/shift-tab/arrow keys/enter/escape as applicable to each control type).
- Focus is never lost or trapped: opening and closing any modal or dialog in the
  audited flows returns focus to the invoking element, and focus order follows the
  visual/logical order of the page.
- Focus indicators are visibly consistent: equivalent controls across the four
  audited flows show the same focus indicator treatment, and every focusable
  control shows a discernible focus indicator.
- Every defect enumerated by the audit report for the four flows is addressed or
  explicitly dispositioned with rationale.
- Keyboard regression checks for the four flows are added to the Dashboard test
  suite so the fixes are guarded against regressions.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with
  no focus traps or unreachable controls — delivered by the focus-trap,
  focus-loss, and reachability fixes above.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — delivered by the focus indicator normalization above, bundled with HLR-1
  because both edit the same flows, dialogs, and UI surfaces.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation —
the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) and the product documentation
accessibility statement — so that both reflect the fixed state of the four core
Dashboard flows after keyboard accessibility remediation. Two public-sector
customers require an updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so
the published documentation itself is a deliverable of the strategy.

## Scope

Content outline (authored inside the Red Hat docs content process):

- Update the VPAT entries for the keyboard operability criteria affected by the
  remediation of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission), including focus management and focus
  indication where the conformance level changed.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the current
  keyboard accessibility state of the audited flows, including any known
  limitations that remain outside this strategy's scope (flows not audited,
  screen-reader semantics beyond the keyboard fixes).
- Republish both artifacts to their published locations so the updated conformance
  statement is publicly available.
- Exclude claims about flows or criteria outside the four audited flows and the
  keyboard scope of the remediation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT conformance entries for the audited flows' keyboard operability reflect
  the post-remediation state, with no claim that is not backed by a verified fix.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated to match the
  post-remediation keyboard accessibility state, and remaining out-of-scope
  limitations are stated accurately.
- Both documents are technically reviewed against the implemented remediation of
  the four audited flows by the engineering owners of that work, with review
  sign-off recorded before publication.
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are republished and reachable at
  their published locations.
- The conformance documentation is deliverable to the public-sector customers as
  an updated published statement (renewal requirement).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review — fully delivered by this epic.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

**Strategy**: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
**Triage**: Not below-threshold — although the strategy is S-sized with a single code
component (Dashboard), the scope spans two architecturally distinct work streams:
keyboard/focus remediation code in the Dashboard, and substantive accessibility
content authoring (VPAT rewrite and accessibility statement republish). The
multiple-distinct-work-streams escape condition applies, so the strategy decomposes
into separate code and content epics. No genuine unknowns: the strategy states the
audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard operability and focus indicator remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001: Keyboard/focus remediation] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002: VPAT and docs republish]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by ALL Implementation epics) | The VPAT and accessibility statement must describe the fixed state, so the documentation epic is blocked by the Dashboard remediation epic. |

No other edges: the remediation epic is a single logical change (see HLR Traceability)
and there are no external dependencies, investigations, or onboarding chains — the
Dashboard is an existing, Konflux-onboarded component per architecture context.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard operability of the four audited flows. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | `bundled` — consistent focus indicators edit the same flows, components, and UI surfaces as the HLR-1 focus-trap/unreachable-control fixes (same modal dialogs, same forms, same CSS/patternfly surface). Splitting HLR-2 into its own epic would double-touch the same files and produce two epics building the same surface, so it stays bundled with HLR-1. Both are P1, so no deferral signal is lost. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | VPAT and accessibility statement update, technical review, and republish. |

All HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: The strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then), and no Non-Functional
  Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria below were derived from the HLRs and
  the problem statement; the strategy should ideally be back-filled with explicit ACs.
- **Team inference**: The strategy does not state owners. The Dashboard epic is
  assigned to RHOAI Dashboard per the architecture context file
  (`architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`, owning team RHOAI Dashboard). The
  documentation epic is assigned to RHOAI Documentation as the Red Hat docs content
  process owner; the technical review AC routes Dashboard engineering sign-off. Verify
  both assignments with the strategy author.
- **Scope trap (low)**: The VPAT is a customer-facing conformance claim. Republishing
  it before the remediation is fully verified would create a compliance exposure — the
  E001 → E002 edge mitigates this, and the E002 acceptance criteria require the
  conformance statement to reflect only verified fixes.
- **Sizing**: E001 bundles the defects of four flows. The audit report enumerates the
  exact defects per flow; if the defect volume for a single flow exceeds roughly a
  sprint of remediation effort, re-split E001 by flow (each flow's fixes touch
  distinct Dashboard pages) rather than by HLR.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing; both epics are
internal and sequential by nature (docs describe the fixed state).

## Criterion Details

### 1. HLR Coverage (2/2)
All three HLRs map to epics: HLR-1 and HLR-2 (both P1) to RHAISTRAT-9017-E001, HLR-3
(P2) to RHAISTRAT-9017-E002. The traceability matrix is present and complete. The

record where the mapping is read: the matrix row is flagged `bundled` with a full
rationale (same flows, modal dialogs, forms, and CSS/patternfly surface; a split would
double-touch the same files and build the same surface twice). Both HLRs are P1, so no
deferral signal is lost — this is not a priority collapse. Priority inheritance is
clean: E001 is P1 matching its HLRs, and E002 is a docs-authoring epic whose P2 derives
from the strategy's Normal priority (Critical→P0, Major→P1, Normal→P2), exempt from
priority inheritance; the E001→E002 Rule 11 edge is not a priority inheritance
violation.

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)
Single edge E001 → E002, justified by Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all
Implementation epics) — the VPAT must describe the fixed state, so the edge is a
genuine content dependency. Frontmatter cross-check: E002's `dependencies` lists
RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 and E001's is empty, matching the diagram exactly (arrow drawn
dependency → dependent, per convention). No circular dependencies, no invalid edges,
no konflux-onboarding / license-validation / repo-onboarding epics so rules 7/8/10 are
vacuous, no conditional branch files. No data/artifact dependency in epic content is
missing from the DAG — the only cross-epic coupling (docs describing the fixed state)
is captured by the single edge. Critical path length 2 fits the S-size heuristic (1-2).

### 3. Epic Boundaries (2/2)
Each epic is a distinct component/team tuple: E001 (Dashboard / RHOAI Dashboard) and
E002 (Documentation / RHOAI Documentation). Work-product types are correctly separated
— code remediation in E001, content authoring (VPAT rewrite, accessibility statement)
in E002 — so there is no code/content mixing. No scope duplication between siblings:
E001 builds the remediation, E002 documents it; neither rebuilds the other's surface,
and the two are not two presentation modes of one surface. E001's size (defects of four
flows in one epic) is a managed watch item, not a defect: the summary's Health Warnings
records a concrete re-split trigger ("if the defect volume for a single flow exceeds
roughly a sprint of remediation effort, re-split E001 by flow"), with the correct
re-split axis (by flow, not by HLR). Per the oversized-epic handling rule this is noted
as managed and no split is suggested.

### 4. Type Correctness (2/2)
Both epics are Implementation and both produce concrete artifacts (remediated flows +
regression tests; published VPAT and accessibility statement). E002 correctly carries
`implementation_type: docs-authoring`; E001 is a general implementation with null
implementation type — appropriate. No Investigation epics exist and the strategy
confirms no genuine unknowns ("the audit report enumerates the exact defects per
flow"), so the absence of investigations is correct, not a gap. No `gated_by` or
`gate_failure_impact` fields are set, and none are needed — no gates exist.

### 5. AI Implementability Scoring (2/2)
Both epics are Implementation type and both carry `ai_signals` (the 9-signal rubric)
with `investigation_signals: null` — the type-appropriate fields. Signal values are
consistent with the strategy content and the rationales in the ai-signals files match
the frontmatter values. Calibration check against `.context`: E001 scores
`architecture_claims: 1` with a rationale citing
`.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md` ("Surfaces data
science projects, workbenches, model serving, pipelines") — correctly calibrated to the
architecture-context file covering the component. E002 scores `architecture_claims: 0`
with the rationale that no architecture-context file covers Documentation — verified
correct: only `dashboard.md` exists under `.context/architecture-context/`, and the
Documentation component is in the canonical list without an architecture context file.
`human_process_gates: -1` on E002 is consistent with the Rule 24 technical-review
sign-off AC; `open_questions: 1` on both epics matches the strategy's "Open Questions:
None". No arithmetic or threshold checking performed (pipeline-computed).

### 6. Acceptance Criteria Quality (2/2)
Both epics have testable, strategy-derived ACs. E001's ACs are concrete and verifiable
(per-flow keyboard completion, no unreachable controls, focus return to invoking
element, consistent indicators, every audit defect addressed or dispositioned,
regression tests added). E002 carries the rule-mandated technical-review AC (review by
the engineering owners of the remediation, sign-off recorded before publication) plus
republish-verification ACs. No soft-ACs: the E002 AC on deliverability to the
public-sector customers is a condition on the epic's own deliverable (the published
statement), not an externally-granted availability precondition. No replacement epic
exists (no rollback/feature-flag AC required) and no konflux chain exists (no
build-pipeline AC required). No epic body references sibling epics by draft ID — E001
refers to "the updated conformance documentation" and E002 to "the engineering owners
of that work" without E-number references.

### 7. Completeness (2/2)
The full strategy scope is covered: all four audited flows (project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission), focus-indicator consistency, the
VPAT update, the accessibility-statement update, technical review, and republish are
all accounted for across the two epics. Out-of-scope boundaries (screen-reader
semantics beyond keyboard fixes, flows outside the four) are explicitly carried into
E001's scope and E002's known-limitations content. Strategy-level context is carried
forward: the public-sector customer renewal requirement appears in E002's description
and ACs, and remaining limitations are stated accurately per E002's scope. The
docs-authoring epic required by the documentation deliverable is present. The
strategy's own missing sections (no Impacted Teams, Dependencies, ACs, or NFRs) are
flagged in the summary's Health Warnings with a back-fill recommendation rather than
silently dropped. No conditional branches exist or are needed (no bounded unknowns).
